## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This pull request adds millisecond timeout parsing, port validation, JSON configuration loading, and hostname normalization. It is not ready to merge because deleting the defaults file breaks the existing startup loader, and several new helpers have correctness, failure-reporting, documentation, and coverage issues.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file leaves `app.startup.load_defaults()` unconditionally reading a nonexistent sibling path; every call to `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError`. — Application startup cannot load its required defaults.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — The strict upper-bound comparison rejects port `65535`, despite the documented valid range being 1–65535. — A service configured on the valid TCP port 65535 is incorrectly rejected.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Catching every `Exception` silently converts missing files, permission errors, malformed JSON, and parser failures into `{}`; for example, a truncated configuration file appears to load successfully. — Deployments can continue with unintended empty configuration while concealing the actionable configuration error.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says an empty hostname “returns None,” while the branch immediately below returns `""`. — Callers following the documented contract can mishandle the empty-host sentinel.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — The hostname test exercises only lowercasing and never covers the trailing-dot branch with an input such as `"Example.COM."`. — A regression that leaves fully qualified hostnames unnormalized could ship unnoticed and cause hostname comparisons to fail.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- Millisecond timeout conversion is covered with a behavior-focused test.
- Successful JSON configuration loading and hostname lowercasing are tested.
- The optional accelerated JSON parser has a clearly documented standard-library fallback.
